Week 12 kicks off with the UCF eyeing a win over Iowa State as slight 1.5-point favorites on Friday, Nov. 20. My Iowa State vs. UCF prediction and college football picks lean toward the Knights' defense keeping the Cyclones' ground attack in check. Kickoff at the Acrisure Bounce House is set for 6 p.m. ET on FS1. Moneyline prediction: UCF Over/Under prediction: Under 49.5 Who will win Iowa State vs UCF: UCF moneyline Screw the points, give me UCF outright on senior night. UCF has been up and down since taking down BYU following the Cougars' upset win over Notre Dame. However, the Knights draw an Iowa State team nearing the end of its first season without Matt Campbell. The Cyclones have leaned on their ground attack all season, running the ball on more than 56% of their plays. However, UCF ranks No. 1 in the Big 12 in fewest explosive rushing plays allowed , per StatRankings . If the Knights can contain the run, they should be able to slow down Iowa State's offense. Interestingly enough, Iowa State has allowed the fourth-fewest explosive passing plays while giving up nearly eight yards per pass attempt and 230 passing yards per game. The Cyclones' defense is surrendering more than 415 total yards per contest, which is a lot of production for a unit that has done a good job limiting big plays. UCF is playable up to 60%. AccuWeather has a flood watch in place from Tuesday at 5 p.m. through Friday at 7 p.m., while The Weather Channel is projecting up to an inch of rain Friday night. Slick conditions could make things difficult for both offenses, especially with two teams that have shown a tendency to get off to slow starts. UCF's rushing attack is one of the worst statistical ground games in the country, while Iowa State relies on running the football on more than 56% of its plays. If the Knights can contain the Cyclones' ground attack, they should have a chance to control the tempo and limit explosive plays. Between the weather concerns, two potentially sluggish offenses, and a lack of urgency on either side, I don't mind looking toward the Under here. UCF vs Iowa State prediction Beating Iowa State is pretty simple: Contain Aiden Flora, and you've got 'em. The third-year sophomore has five games in which he's gone over 100 yards. In those games, his lowest output was 182 yards in a 42-31 defense-optional shootout against Baylor two weeks ago. The Cyclones are 4-0 in those other games, three of which saw Flora surpass 200 yards on the ground. He's racked up a ridiculous 619 yards and six touchdowns over the past three games, adding eight catches for 58 yards as well as a pair of pass completions (only one went for anything, a 37-yarder last week vs. Cincinnati). UCF's run defense ranks eighth in the 16-team Big 12 at just under 137 yards per game. They held Arizona State to 3.6 yards per carry last week but surrendered nearly 5 ypc and four touchdowns to Kansas in a winning effort the week prior. Arkansas State transfer Jaylen Raynor has led the Big 12's worst passing offense at just under 207 yards per game, but even he's played better in recent weeks amid Flora's ascension, throwing for 794 yards and six TDs against just two interceptions. The Knights can absolutely win on Senior Night. The run game was stifled by Arizona State, but UCF was without lead back Duke Watson, and Iowa State has the third-worst run-stopping unit in the Big 12. If everyone is back and healthy, and if Alonza Barnett can complement that with some timely strikes, the Knights can get the win. The Cyclones haven't won any of their four road games this season, but three of those teams (Iowa, BYU and Arizona) are ranked. A bowl berth might come down to the final week, just like it did in 2023. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: Iowa State Cyclones @ UCF Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 19, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Big 12 UCF and Iowa State battle for bowl eligibility at the Bounce House, while Aiden Flora is on a hot streak. Time and date: Friday, November 20 at 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: UCF (-2.5) Over/under: 49.5 All-time series: Iowa State leads, 1-0 Last meeting: Iowa State 38, UCF 35 — October 19, 2024 Current streak: Iowa State, 1 (2024) Setting the scene Friday night football kicks off early this week. At 6 p.m. ET, the Bounce House welcomes Iowa State for the first time as two 5-5 Big 12 opponents compete for bowl eligibility. UCF has been the master of chaotic finishes this season, recently shocking BYU in double overtime and upending Kansas with a game-winning touchdown on the final snap. Iowa State has also escaped a handful of close finishes this year, sliding past West Virginia in a back-and-forth finish before kicking a game-winning field goal on Halloween to upset Oklahoma State. With two teams accustomed to close finishes chasing that coveted sixth win, and a potential Heisman finisher involved, Friday night in Orlando should feature no shortage of drama. Iowa State Cyclones outlook Iowa State (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) has been as battle-tested as anyone in college football this season. The Cyclones already faced four teams ranked in the top 20 of the latest College Football Playoff rankings. They’ve also defeated three Big 12 opponents with records of 5-5 or greater, eking out close wins over West Virginia and Oklahoma State before blowing the doors of Cincinnati last Saturday. There have been two different versions of the Cyclones in year one under Jimmy Rogers. In Ames, Iowa State is a force to be reckoned with, posting a 5-1 home record with a lone defeat to No. 2 Utah. Yet, the Cyclones remain in search of their first road victory under Rogers, although all four of their road opponents are currently 6-4 or better. Iowa State’s success is largely correlated with the performance of Doak Walker Award semifinalist Aiden Flora. The running back has catapulted into the No. 1 spot on the nation’s rushing leaderboard at 1,335 yards, thanks to three consecutive 180+ yard explosions. Flora has an FBS-best five 180-yard games this year, including three performances where he eclipsed 210 yards. The versatile sophomore is a touchdown machine, and his scoring ability isn’t limited to just the run game. In addition to producing 12 rushing touchdowns, Flora has thrown two passing touchdowns and recorded a punt return touchdown, and he also ranks second on the team in receptions. The explosive Flora has four 60-yard runs this year, a total topped by just three FBS programs. His ability opens up things for the passing game, which has a commensalistic relationship with the future All-Big 12 running back. All three of Jaylen Raynor’s 250-yard showings through the air occurred when Flora crossed 180 on the ground. The mobile quarterback has been able to stretch the field more vertically as of late. He has started 10 games this season, yet 42 percent of his passing yards and 46 percent of his passing touchdowns occurred in the last three weeks. Raynor has established a strong connection with true freshman Jamal Polite Jr., who averages 19.5 yards per reception as the premier downfield threat. But what happens when Flora goes under 180? Iowa State has struggled when it gets behind the sticks. The Cyclones are 113th nationally in third down offense, and Iowa State has converted just 20-of-71 (28.2 percent) third downs across its five losses. The Cyclones have been inconsistent on defense. They enjoyed strong performances against BYU and Cincinnati but allowed at least 39 points in four of their last six contests. Iowa State ranks 108th in total defense, struggling particularly against the run where it allows 174 yards per game on a 4.93 average. Inside linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has been one of the unit’s key playmakers, checking in at third in the Big 12 with 93 tackles. However, the Cyclones are severely lacking in two categories on defense: sacks and interceptions. They rank 100th in the FBS with 1.6 sacks per game, and defensive end Isaac Terrell leads the unit with 3.5 — producing three of those sacks in the Sept. 5 opener. Additionally, Iowa State has only picked off two passes all season, and two were courtesy of middle linebacker Beau Goodwin. Thus, the secondary looks to make more havoc plays and avoid these high-scoring shootout style games moving forward. UCF Knights outlook UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is on the brink of its second bowl appearance since joining the Big 12 in 2023. The Knights are the last remaining program that has yet to produce a winning record as a member of the conference, but the opportunity to end the drought presents itself this November. Since stunning then-No. 2 BYU in overtime on Oct. 24, the Knights are 0-2 at home, dropping lopsided contests to Baylor and Arizona State. All four of UCF’s Big 12 losses came by at least 10 points, while all three wins were by single-digits, as the Knights have shown the ability to prosper in tightly-contested games. To qualify for bowl eligibility, UCF must jumpstart its offense which has scored 22 points across its last two games at the Bounce House. The Knights recently returned to their original starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 at Pittsburgh. Barnett has won 13 of his last 16 starts, and the senior has elevated the passing attack, surpassing 250 passing yards in both starts this November. Barnett’s presence on the field has turned wide receiver Josh Derry into a budding star. In his past two games, Derry has hauled in 15 receptions for 280 yards and a touchdown, emerging as the top receiver in this offense. True freshman Tyren Hornes is also making strides, registering 59 receiving yards (his second-highest total of the season) and his second career touchdown against the Sun Devils. However, the Knights must improve their pass protection, as they rank 113th nationally with 2.7 sacks allowed per game. That correlates to an unsatisfying third down conversion rate of 34.4 percent, which sits one spot below Iowa State on the national leaderboard. But perhaps the greatest struggle for UCF’s offense — which is also related to the offensive line — is the decline of the run game. The Knights haven’t produced a 100-yard rusher since Week 3, or a 60-yard rusher in each of their last three games. No UCF running back has rattled off a 20-yard run since Oct. 24, and the Knights look to create lanes for Duke Watson, Landen Chambers, and Taevion Swint to break that streak. The Knights are typically strong starters on defense, and they have yet to allow more than seven points in a first quarter this season. However, finishing games is a priority for a unit that allowed 25 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Kansas and 27 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Houston. UCF continues to operate without one of its top defenders in strong safety Demari Henderson, who suffered an injury late in the BYU game on Oct. 24. Still, there is veteran talent across the secondary including cornerback Antione Jackson, whose 10 pass breakups lead the Big 12, and cornerback Jayden Williams, who ranks second on the team with 53 tackles, in addition to recording one interception and two forced fumbles. While the Knights are better than the Cyclones in turnover production, they similarly struggle in getting to opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Isaiah Nixon leads UCF with 2.5 sacks on the season, and the team has gone consecutive weeks without registering a sack. Despite the offenses trending in different directions, UCF opens as a slight favorite over Iowa State, largely due to the location of the game. The Knights recorded two of their three Big 12 wins at the Bounce House, while the Cyclones have been futile away from home this year. The plamayking of Aiden Flora will be the main determinant in this matchup. Flora recorded over 100 rushing yards and three touchdowns in the first quarter last week, almost single-handedly putting Cincinnati away in 15 minutes. UCF’s defense must be prepared to counter the running back in any way possible. Stacking the box isn’t always an ideal strategy, because Iowa State loves to catch defenses off-guard with his pop passes. The Cyclones will keep things creative on offense, and UCF must remain disciplined defensively beyond the first quarter. Iowa State sustains its offensive rhythm from the last three weeks, while the Knights struggle to find openings for their run game. The end result: the Cyclones become bowl eligible in Jimmy Rogers’ debut season. The Knights are 1.5-point home favorites in a matchup between two teams looking to secure bowl eligibility. Iowa State enters the game following a dominant 41-13 victory over Cincinnati, led by Aiden Flora's 216 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Meanwhile, UCF is coming off a disappointing 26-13 loss to Arizona State. The Cyclones have struggled away from home this season, while the Knights have been much more competitive in Orlando. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:00 p.m. CT on FS1. Below, we'll break down the latest Iowa State vs. UCF odds, where to watch, key injuries and expected starters, along with our prediction and pick for this Friday night Big 12 showdown. Iowa State vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 54.5 points Moneyline: UCF -112 | Iowa State -108 Odds reported November 15, 2026. Lines subject to change. Where to Watch Iowa State vs. UCF Date: Friday, November 20, 2026 Kickoff: 5:00 p.m. CT / 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Florida Streaming: FOX Sports app with an eligible TV subscription Iowa State vs. UCF Injuries and Expected Starters Iowa State is expected to start Jaylen Raynor at quarterback, while running back Aiden Flora enters Friday's matchup following one of the best performances of his season. Flora rushed for 216 yards and three touchdowns against Cincinnati, bringing his season total to more than 1,100 rushing yards. For UCF, the quarterback situation is worth monitoring. Keyone Jenkins has dealt with an ankle injury, while Alonza Barnett III has also seen action at quarterback. Jenkins was listed as a game-time decision ahead of the Arizona State game, making his availability an important storyline heading into Friday. UCF running back Duke Watson was listed as unavailable against Arizona State, while Iowa State quarterback Connor Moberly was also listed as out against Cincinnati. The official Big 12 availability report for this matchup has not yet been released. This section will be updated as additional injury information becomes available. Iowa State vs. UCF Biggest Question: Who Stops the Run? Both teams would like to try and establish the run. Iowa State is led by star running back Aiden Flora, while UCF has a more balanced approach to the running attack, led by Duke Watson. Iowa State's offense has been far superior this season, ranking No. 28 in the country in yards per play, while UCF's offense is outside of the Top 100. However, it's UCF's defense that ranks in the Top 60 in yards per play, while Iowa State is outside the Top 100. Whoever wins this battle will have the leg up in this game on Friday night. Iowa State vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: Iowa State 27, UCF 23 Pick against the spread: Iowa State +1.5 Both teams have been better at home vs. the on the road, which is the only reason I am hesitant on this game for the Cyclones. I also don't want to overreact to their huge performance vs. Cincinnati last week. A road game on a Friday night is a much toughest spot. That being the case, UCF just hasn't earned my money in this spot, or the right to be a favorite. And it feels like the offense has either taken a step back, or just gotten confused since it had to move to back to Alonza Barnett at QB compared to where it was with Keyone Jenkins. UCF is last in the Big 12 in first downs and 15th in third-down conversions. And while Iowa State's defense hasn't been great, they've also played some of the most explosive offenses in the Big 12, like Utah, Arizona and Oklahoma State. I think that side of the ball can exceed expectations against a UCF offense that has been far from consistent. Iowa State vs. UCF FAQ What time is Iowa State vs. UCF? picks.blurb: Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? IowaStateRoundtable 17 Members • 193 Posts IowaStateRoundtable IowaStateRoundtable Related stories Trending stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? Brad Schultz Partner Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM Published Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM This matchup between 5-5 teams should be an all-out fight for bowl eligibility. Here's how Publisher Brad Schultz sees this one playing out. More Videos No one expected Iowa State football to be in the position it's in right now, and why would they? Jimmy Rogers had to rebuild this Cyclone program from the ground up after Matt Campbell left for Penn State and gutted the roster in the process. Some programs can endure such a teardown and instantly be in the national spotlight the following season, but few thought it could be done at Iowa State, one of the losingest Power Four college football programs. While it's certainly not all cupcakes and rainbows in Ames right now, the Cyclones currently sit at 5-5 – one win away from an improbable trip to a bowl game. But there's no time for Iowa State to celebrate just yet. It has two games to finish the job and get at least one win to secure bowl eligibility and continue its sudden momentum. The first game on the docket takes place on Friday against UCF. The Knights are also 5-5, so this matchup has the potential to be an all-out war in what looks to be soggy Florida weather in Orlando. Related stories More content will be coming out on Thursday, but in the meantime, here's how I see this matchup playing out. Matchup: Iowa State Cyclones (5-5, 3-4) @ UCF Knights (5-5, 3-4) Location: Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Florida Scheduled game time: Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. CDT Weather: 72 degrees with rain (flash flood warning have been issued) Announcers: Noah Reed (play-by-play) and Petros Papadakis (analyst) Radio: Cyclone Radio Network (John Walters, Eric Heft) Betting information (as of Nov. 18 and per DraftKings): UCF -2.5 | O/U: 48.5 As I've been saying all week, I feel like this is an extremely winnable game for Iowa State. While UCF does boast a really good win over BYU, the Knights have been extremely inconsistent under Scott Frost (who folks in the state of Iowa should know by now). They've alternated wins and losses since the dramatic win over the Cougars on Oct. 24 – a 41-9 drubbing at the hands of Baylor one week after the BYU victory, a last-second touchdown to beat Kansas, and a 13-point home loss to an Arizona State team that had to fly to Orlando the day of the game. Long story short, what UCF team are we going to see on Friday? We really don't know, and that's why I trust Iowa State in this spot. There's probably going to be a nice dose of cardinal and gold inside the Bounce House for this game, but that's not the only reason why I'm picking the Cyclones. The other reason why this game favors Iowa State is the weather. It's going to be a rainy slugfest in Orlando, but the Cyclones have the pleasure of having Aiden Flora on their team. He's doing incredible things every week and should get plenty of carries with a likely run-first game plan here. Neither defense is very good, but Flora is going to be the difference yet again. The Cyclones clinch bowl eligibility in the Sunshine State. Prediction: Iowa State 31, UCF 23

away.headline: Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly suspended for a game for `inappropriate contact' with player
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Fennelly will sit out at Northern Iowa on Wednesday night. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will direct the team that night. AMES, Iowa (AP) — Iowa State suspended women’s basketball coach Bill Fennelly one game Sunday night for “inappropriate contact” with a Cyclones player. Fennelly nudged the player’s head with his hand earlier Sunday in a 69-64 home victory over Illinois Chicago. The 69-year-old Bill Fennelly said last month he plans to retire at the end of the season, his 32nd as head coach at the school. “We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not,” athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. “We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions.” “I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game,” Fennelly said in a statement. “I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward.” The Cyclones are 5-0 this season. Fennelly is 661-335 with 24 NCAA Tournament appearances and 26 postseason appearances at Iowa State. 'GTA 6' impacts sports RB Duke Watson Headlines UCF Injury Report Ahead of Arizona State Game (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:42 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Running back Duke Watson headlines a lengthy UCF Knights injury report ahead of their home game against the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday. Watson was carted off the field in last Saturday's thriller win over the Kansas Jayhawks . He wore street clothes and a boot on his right foot on the sidelines. Coach Scott Frost couldn't provide an update on the junior's status in his weekly press conference on Monday. Frost said he'd learn more Monday evening, and now the Knights will be without their speedster workhorse. The junior has 596 yards and three touchdowns on 94 carries this season. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

Ohio State is 14th in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, but it's still knee-deep in the hunt if it gets a little bit of help. Yes, the Cornhuskers have been in a down cycle for two-plus decades. But it's hard to believe a program still among the winningest in history hasn't beaten a ranked opponent since a 35-32 win over Oregon on Sept. 17, 2016. Only Rutgers, at 46 in a row, has a longer losing streak against the Top 25. The Huskers' skid has covered the coaching runs of Mike Riley, Scott Frost, interim coach Mickey Joseph and now Matt Rhule, whose personal losing streak against the Top 25 stands at 21 over a combined seven seasons at Baylor and Nebraska. Nebraska nearly broke through against then-No. 7 Indiana on Oct. 10. The Huskers entered the fourth quarter leading by 11 points and lost 20-17. The next opportunity comes Saturday when No. 16 Ohio State visits. If the Huskers lose, they will presumably get another chance the day after Thanksgiving at Iowa, which is No. 13 this week. All games are on Saturday unless noted: No. 1 Georgia (minus 16 1/2) at South Carolina Bulldogs are rolling right now and the injuries are piling up for South Carolina, which was without QB LaNorris Sellers in last week's loss to Arkansas. Pick: Georgia 38-14. No. 2 Utah (minus 7) at TCU Aside from BYU, this will be the toughest defense the unbeaten Utes have faced. Horned Frogs' problem is offense, or lack of it. Pick: Utah 24-13. Mustangs won't win, but they won't let the game get away from them like they did in last week's 42-point home loss to Wake Forest. Pick: Notre Dame 33-20. No. 4 UCLA (minus 3 1/2) at Michigan Unbeaten Bruins have been better on road than at home. Wolverines have major injury issues, and their 24-point loss to Oregon was their most lopsided in six years. Pick: UCLA 27-21. Virginia Tech (plus 21) at No. 5 Miami Hokies have allowed 91 points while getting clobbered two weeks in a row, and another sound beating is in store if they don't shore things up. Pick: Miami 35-17. Pick: Indiana 26-14. Arkansas at No. 8 Texas (minus 20 1/2) Longhorns won't let last week's comeback win at LSU go to waste against an Arkansas team that's lost 14 straight road games against ranked SEC opponents. Pick: Texas 34-10. LSU (minus 1) at No. 9 Tennessee It's all about the run game for Tennessee, and Tigers have held three straight and seven of 10 opponents under 100 yards on the ground. Pick: LSU 24-21. No. 10 Wake Forest (minus 20 1/2) at Georgia Tech Demon Deacons' 44-points-per-game offense goes against a Georgia Tech defense allowing 43 per game against ACC opponents excluding last week's 20-6 win at Clemson. Pick: Wake Forest 45-20. Pick: Texas Tech 33-27. No. 12 BYU at Kansas (plus 5 1/2) Cougars' playoff hopes depend on their defense's ability to keep dual-threat QB Isaiah Marshall under control. Pick: BYU 27-24. No. 13 Iowa (minus 8) at Illinois Carson Boyd, with 22 career snaps, could make his first start for Illinois against a top-10 Iowa defense that leads nation in red zone defense. Pick: Iowa 31-17. No. 14 Oregon (minus 16) at Michigan State Ducks comes into the Friday night game leading Big Ten in pass plays of 20-plus yards, and Spartans are prone to giving up big chunks through the air. Pick: Oregon 36-19. San Diego State at No. 15 Boise State (minus 16 1/2) Broncos QB Maddux Madsen had a career game against Oregon State in his first game back from injury. Aztecs are giving up more than 500 yards and 47 points per game on the road. Pick: Boise State 52-28. No. 16 Ohio State at Nebraska (plus 3) The time has come for Cornhuskers to end their 31-game losing streak against AP Top 25 opponents. Their defense will make it happen. Pick: Nebraska 24-21. No. 17 Kentucky (plus 5 1/2) at Missouri Both have lost two in a row and faded from the playoff picture. Kentucky allowed total of 451 rushing yards to Tennessee and Florida. Run game has been Mizzou's strength, but not as much lately. Pick: Missouri 27-26. Maryland at No. 18 Southern California (minus 17 1/2) Terrapins have won two straight under interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim. They haven't won three in a row in conference play since 2006. Pick: USC 41-21. Mountaineers tandem of Cam Cook and Michael Hawkins, averaging a combined 203 yards per game on the ground, were shut down by Kansas. Pick: Houston 44-41. Pittsburgh (plus 14) at No. 21 Louisville Cardinals need to ratchet up their offense. They will play first half without leading tackler Stanquan Clark, who was suspended for his role in postgame fracas with North Carolina. Pick: Louisville 26-17. Western Kentucky at No. 22 Liberty (minus 17) Liberty should be able to unleash its Conference USA-best run game against a defense giving up more than 5 yards per rushing attempt. Pick: Liberty 42-21. Vanderbilt at No. 23 Florida (minus 13 1/2) Everything is contingent on which version of the Gators show up — the one that's beaten three ranked opponents or the one soundly beaten at home by South Carolina and Oklahoma. Pick: Florida 29-14. No. 24 Memphis (minus 3 1/2) at Navy Marcus Stokes, who has four straight 300-yard passing games, will be the difference in a game featuring top-10 rushing offenses. Sayin suffered a fractured elbow in the fourth quarter against Indiana after being brought down on a sack. He initially returned to the sideline with his right arm in a sling before Ohio State confirmed he would be unavailable indefinitely. He subsequently underwent surgery. Day did not provide a specific return date or confirm whether Sayin would play again this season. Will Julian Sayin Return This Season? A return during the regular season appears unlikely. Ohio State has been preparing to finish its remaining schedule without its starting quarterback, and Sayin was officially listed as out ahead of Saturday's matchup against Northwestern. home.headline: Nebraska’s OSU injury report is rough, but Anthony Jones' return could be bright spot
home.blurb: Defensive back Andrew Marshall is out , as Matt Rhule announced earlier this week that one of the nation's top cornerbacks will miss the rest of Nebraska’s season. The good news for the Huskers is that defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. was upgraded from “out” last week to “questionable” this week. With this being the first injury report of the week, there’s now hope that he could be upgraded to probable by Friday and then suit up on Saturday morning. For Ohio State, the guys who are out were all expected to be out. Quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja'Kobi Jackson, safety Deshawn Stewart, wide receiver Brennen Schramm, offensive linemen Jaxon Powell and Max Riley, and tight end Maxence LeBlanc will miss the game against the Cornhuskers. Nebraska football loses Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington but Anthony Jones could return The Ohio State players who are questionable are safety Terry Moore, wide receiver Brock Boyd, safety Brenten "Inky" Jones, linebacker Eli Lee, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels. The biggest piece of positive news for the Buckeyes is that senior left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to return. Montgomery is ready to roll after not appearing on the report, while both Daniels and Boyd are listed as questionable. Montgomery and Daniels had flu-like symptoms last week, while Boyd has been battling a sprained ankle for more than a month. No surprises popped up on the availability report for Ohio State, unlike last week when Montgomery was initially listed as questionable. That suggests the Buckeyes avoided any major new injuries in their win over Northwestern. Of course, the biggest absence of all for OSU is quarterback Julian Sayin. That might not be as big a problem for Ryan Day and company after his replacement, Luke Fahey , finally had a very solid outing. Against Northwestern, Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also threw an interception, but the biggest step forward was that he seemed to figure out a secret to the offense: Just get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. Without Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington, and Andrew Marshall, Nebraska will have its work cut out for it on Saturday morning. This article was originally published on huskercorner.com as Nebraska’s OSU injury report is rough, but Anthony Jones' return could be bright spot . picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. away.blurb: Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3) suffered a frustrating 24-21 loss Saturday at Maryland (4-6, 2-5), a result that only intensified questions surrounding the program's direction . Having already handed out grades for the offense , Badgers On SI now breaks down the defense and special teams. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. home.headline: 'Stop investing in average guys': Boilermaker great Bernard Pollard rips Purdue football
home.blurb: “They’re trying to put a product out there, but I just don’t think the product is good enough,” Pollard said. “I’m just being frank. They said this guy they brought in was more Tiller-like, but you want to see something happen. With the way football is now, you need to win now.” Purdue closes out its home slate on Saturday, hosting Wisconsin. The Boilers haven't beaten the Badgers since Pollard was a freshman (2003), losing 18 straight games in the series. Why One Quote From Barry Odom's Week 12 Press Conference Stood Out If you've been disgruntled with Purdue's football program over the last four years, you're not alone. Boilermaker great and Super Bowl champion Bernard Pollard has been unimpressed with his school's performance on the field. Pollard, who played at Purdue under Joe Tiller from 2003 to 2005 and was a second-team All-Big Ten selection in 2004, hasn't been pleased with the way the school has handled coaching searches or maintaining relationships with alumni. “I feel for the coaches, but at the same time, if you’re a coach, you know the deal,” Pollard told Kyle Odegard of Rotogrinders.com in an exclusive interview . “For Purdue’s sake, they need to hire really good coaches. Stop investing in these average guys. They need to go get somebody who can get these boys playing ball, get alumni there. "Purdue has done a terrible job, an absolutely awful job with alumni and getting people in. If they get rid of this dude, I might need to put my name in the hat, because I can coach.” After reaching the Big Ten Championship Game in 2022, the Boilermakers have fallen to the bottom of the Big Ten. Ryan Walters was fired after just two seasons as head coach, going 5-19 duirng his time in West Lafayette. Following his firing in 2024, Purdue brought in Barry Odom to try to turn things around. The Boilers went 2-10 last season and currently sit 3-7 after getting to 3-3 in mid-October. With Wisconsin and Indiana still on the schedule, there's a chance Odom's record is the same as Walters' after two seasons at Purdue. With a strong haul from the transfer portal and a solid recruiting class, the expectations was that Purdue would take a significant step forward in Year 2 of the Odom era. Early in the season, it looked like the Boilers were on that path. Despite some disappointing losses, Purdue posted back-to-back wins over Illinois and Minnesota, getting their first Big Ten victories since the 2023 campaign. Since then, though, Purdue has falled off a cliff. The Boilermakers lost games to Washington, Penn State and Maryland in consecutive weeks. All three earned their first conference win of 2026 against the Boilers. Last weekend, Purdue suffered a 28-7 loss at the hands of Iowa. Sure, Purdue still has a lot of room to grow, but this program could easily be sitting with four or five wins and still in the hunt for bowl eligibility heading into the final two weeks of the season. ACC Football Injury Report: Georgia Tech Lists 17 Out, Stanford 15 North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night's 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina's nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels' backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina's first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone's first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas' production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina's leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. Because he was limited in practice, there's some doubt he'll be able to play against the Cavaliers, but it all depends on how the rest of the week shapes up. I know a lot of college football fans who root for teams outside the SEC get annoyed by the league playing so many FCS opponents in November, but I've long maintained it's a smart way to do things. Teams need "off" weeks more later in the season than they do in September, so the SEC teams that save these games for later in the year are scheduling smarter. The other benefit of the SEC's cupcake weekend is it never fails to remind me that the regular season is damn near finished. Seriously, I get so caught up in the rhythm and non-stop nature of the season once it begins that it becomes difficult to keep track of time. Plus, with games being played on Tuesday and Wednesday nights starting in October, damn near every day starts to feel the same. Perhaps for some of you the changing temperatures, leaves falling off trees, and setting your clocks back an hour probably serve as markers for the passage of time, but not me. I'm stuck inside most of the time working, so the fact that it's getting dark out earlier, or that it's colder, means nothing to me. But when I see that Alabama is playing Chattanooga ? Buddy, that's when I know Thanksgiving is almost here, and that I better start doing my Christmas shopping. So, thank you for your service, SEC. Even if not everybody appreciates what you're doing this weekend, know that I do. Games of the Week No. 4 UCLA at Michigan : This game is a tale of two teams under first-year head coaches that have worked out in much different ways. Bob Chesney has turned UCLA into one of the year's surprise stories. Sure, in the offseason people made all the same "next Indiana " comparisons, but nobody thought it would be true. Yet, here we are, and UCLA is 10-0, leading the Big Ten, and a win away from clinching a Big Ten Championship Game appearance, and probably a College Football Playoff berth to go with it. Michigan? Yeah, well, everybody at Michigan is ready for the season to end. Kyle Whittingham has not been the steadying hand anyone expected, and the Wolverines need a win here or against Ohio State next week to gain bowl eligibility. Not that I expect anybody involved in the program would be super excited to play in the game. As for this matchup, while Michigan hasn't been great, I don't believe this is a great matchup for UCLA. The Bruins aren't complicated. They play good defense, run the ball, and look for opportunities to find explosives in the passing game. Michigan's defense is great at stopping the run and limiting explosive plays. For all the problems the team has had, the defense has been rather consistent. While Oregon had success moving the ball on it last week, the Bruins don't have the same level of talent as the Ducks, and I'm not convinced they'll find the same success. Plus, when UCLA has played defenses with NFL talent like Michigan's, they haven't been incredible. On the other side, Michigan's offense is bad, and has been against everyone. I don't see that changing this week, either. It'll probably be a close game, but only because neither team is likely to score a whole lot. The Pick: Under 38.5 (-120) at Fanduel No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina : There are some unknown factors about this game that make it a little more difficult to figure out. The primary concern is the status of South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers . He didn't play last week against Arkansas , and it turns out Sellers is pretty important to the Gamecocks' operation, as they lost 34-6 without him! And if Arkansas can do that to the Cocks, imagine what Georgia might do! Still, while the Sellers injury was the headliner, he wasn't the only player Carolina was missing. Receivers Nyck Harbor and Nitro Tuggle missed the game, and Mazeo Bennett Jr . left the game with an injury. Harber and Bennett are Carolina's leading receivers, and if their status is in question, it limits the Gamecocks even further. All of which means that it's hard to go against Georgia here. Even though it's a night game at Williams-Brice Stadium, which is one of the more underrated environments in the sport, the Bulldogs just look like the best team in the country, and have for a while. Also, how fired up will South Carolina be for this game? Last week's loss ended any playoff hopes they had. If Georgia gets off to a good start, you can't ignore the possibility that Carolina just checks out of the game and Georgia steamrolls them. The Pick: Georgia -14.5 (-112) at DraftKings Lock of the Week Virginia Tech at No. 7 Miami : Miami needed about two quarters to figure out how to survive on offense without Malachi Toney . Notre Dame held the Canes to 3 points in the first half of their game two weeks ago, and Miami has scored 57 points in six quarters since. Now they're at home against a Virginia Tech team with a defense that hasn't been able to stop anybody lately. I mean, when you're allowing 51 points to SMU, it's not ideal, but it's somewhat understandable. SMU has shown an ability to score points in a hurry. But then the next thing you know, the Mustangs are being held to seven points by Wake Forest and Virginia Tech is letting Stanford score 40 against it. At home! That's the most points Stanford has scored in an ACC game since joining the league in 2024. It's also 12 more points than they had scored in an ACC road game (their previous best came in a 59-28 loss at NC State in 2024). So we have a Miami team that is still playing for a bye and will only impress the committee with blowout wins to finish against a Virginia Tech defense that can't stop anybody right now. The Pick: Miami Team Total Over 40.5 (-125) at DraftKings Waterfowl of the Week No. 13 Oregon at Michigan State : A lot of people stopped paying attention to Oregon in September, and the few who hung on after that mostly checked out following the 21-10 loss to Illinois in October. I'm grateful for it, because it's not often you get the chance to see a team that was a favorite to win the national title before a season suddenly flying under the radar, and the Ducks are definitely flying under the radar. I'm telling you, and I've been saying it for a few weeks now, this team has a chance to get to the playoffs, and if they do, they will be the "Cinderella" of the tournament. They have looked like the Oregon we all expected the last three weeks. They hit our Lock of the Week on their team total over last week, and that was despite dropping a touchdown. Now they're on the road against a Michigan State team that won't have its starting QB, and could be down to its third-string if Cam Fancher isn't able to get healthy in time. The Spartans have been ravaged by injuries most of the year, and while they've been able to muck it up at times, I don't think they have the horses to do it against these Ducks. Especially when Oregon understands simply winning games won't be enough. They have to win by impressive margins to climb into an at-large spot. And I think they'll do so this weekend. The Pick: Oregon -16.5 (-110) at Fanduel Sad Bet of the Week Northern Illinois at North Dakota State : I never want a team to go through a season without a win. When you consider the amount of work coaches and players put into their seasons, the idea of a team never getting to celebrate a single win breaks my damn heart. I want Northern Illinois -- the only winless team remaining on the FBS level -- to get a win, but I do not see it happening this week. It'll have to wait until the regular season finale against 1-9 UTEP . This week, they aren't going into the Fargodome and taking down the Bison. I don't want to go with the spread here, though, because I don't much like the number, and it's possible the Bison will just look to get out of here with the win and slow things down in the second half. Still, it's tough to imagine the Huskies will find much success on offense in this one. The line is basically asking if I think NIU can get to double digits on offense, and my answer is no, I do not. The Pick: Northern Illinois Team Total Under 8.5 (-111) at Fanduel Upset of the Week Syracuse at Boston College : Boston College got destroyed by Notre Dame 41-7 last week. They've lost three straight, including another 47-2 blowout loss on the road to Duke three weeks ago. I don't think this team is all that good. But you know what? I don't think Syracuse is all that good, either. At least not good enough that I would ever feel confident backing the Orange as a road favorite. Because while BC isn't great, it hasn't been awful at home. It's 3-2 at home with wins over Rutgers and Pitt. The two losses came by seven points apiece against Virginia Tech and Florida State . (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan football season felt over when the Wolverines lost to Michigan State, and that defeat seems to have had a similar impact on the team. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. The Wolverines haven't been shutout at home since 1967, but that could change this weekend. UCLA wins, 17-0 UCLA is great defensively, but the Bruins have only eclipsed 30 points once with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback, so I expect Michigan's defense to keep this one relatively close. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.

Now, in just its third year as a Big Ten school, UCLA can go to the Big Ten Championship game with one more win in its last two games. Michigan is looking for anything positive at this point. The season crashed through the floor, going 2-5 in Big Ten play – losing to Oregon and Michigan State by a combined score of 46-13 – and now it needs a win in the last two games just to go to a bowl game. UCLA vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan closes with a bang: losing to Oregon 31-7 last week in Eugene, hosting UCLA this week, and finishing with the showdown against Ohio State in Columbus. UCLA closes at USC next week. It won't need the win if it can beat the Wolverines, but obviously, it's the rivalry game the Bruins want. The two teams haven't played since 2000, a 23-20 UCLA win. Starting in 1956 with a 42-13 win, UCLA is 8-3 in the series. The Wolverines will come out fired up and cranked for the moment, marching down the field with a stunningly crisp opening scoring drive. But UCLA doesn't panic. The Bruin defense will be a rock on third downs, the offense will take the field goals and points when they're available, and Michigan's offense won't be able to take care of its opportunities to pull off the upset. away.headline: Blake Frazer, Rod Moore, Andrew Marsh Headline Michigan's Initial Injury Report vs. UCLA
away.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Kyle Whittingham said so on Monday, but it's very concerning to see the likes of Andrew Marsh, and even Channing Goodwin to a certain extent on the list. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. 'GTA 6' impacts sports Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. Tennessee's College Football Playoff hopes are on the line this weekend against LSU. If the Vols beat LSU on Saturday in Neyland Stadium, they'll just need a win in the regular-season finale against Vanderbilt to lock down a spot in the College Football Playoff. But if Tennessee loses to LSU, they can likely kiss their playoff hopes goodbye. LSU, which has four losses, is out of the playoff picture. The Tigers' 6-4 record, however, isn't indicative of how good of a team they are. LSU has arguably the most talented roster in the nation, and they are just a couple of plays away from being 8-2. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Combine that with the fact that Tennessee will be without several key players against the Tigers — specifically left guard Nic Moore and wide receiver Mike Matthews — and it's easy to see why there's some concern about this game on Rocky Top. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. "This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations," said Murray. "And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. "… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game." I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Tennessee has dealt with terrible injury luck this season — the Vols have had 10 season-ending injuries — but they're still in contention for a College Football Playoff spot with two weeks remaining in the regular season. All Tennessee needs to do is beat LSU and Vanderbilt and they'll lock up a spot in the playoff. First up is LSU. The Tigers are 6-4 and out of the playoff conversation, but they have a talented and dangerous roster that is as good as any team in the nation when they're at their best. Former Georgia pass rusher David Pollack makes prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia standout David Pollack made his pick for the matchup between the Vols and the Tigers. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Pollack likes what he's seen from Tennessee this season, but he thinks the Volunteers have too many injuries to win this game. So, Pollack has LSU winning by a field goal. "Tennessee is hurt everywhere," said Pollack . "Tennessee's beat to death. If Tennessee wins this game, holy cow, man. I mean, that's how much the injuries have been such a big issue for them across the board. Whether it's the quarterback, Mike Matthews at wide receiver, the offensive line, a pass rusher — Tennessee's lost a significant player at almost every spot on the field. That's hard to overcome. "… They've (LSU) been in these games. It's been competitive, and it's been different ways they've beaten themselves. I think the injuries just eat up Tennessee, and I think LSU finds a way to make a few more plays with the ability of Sam Leavitt to scramble against this defensive line. And I think [LSU's] ability to run tempo and kind of wear you out — Tennessee can do the same exact thing, but I think LSU's got more bodies. I just think they've got more availability. I think this is a low-scoring affair — like every Tennessee game is — but I think LSU wins by a field goal." If it's a close game late, I like Tennessee's chances better than LSU's — simply because the Vols have been better at closing games in the fourth quarter than the Tigers have. But I agree with Pollack that Tennessee's injuries are a concern. The Vols have lost a significant number of playmakers, and losing Mike Matthews, Tennessee's top offensive playmaker, is a massive concern against an offense like LSU's. I mean, this is a game where the Vols are probably going to have to throw it a bit more than they have in most games this season in order to win. Can they do that without Matthews? The one thing I'll say about Tennessee this season is that every time they've had an injury, the next man up has delivered. So I'm not doubting Tennessee's ability to get it done against LSU, I just wonder if they'll be healthy enough to find a way. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.blurb: College Football Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Pull up a schedule. Any schedule. Take a look at what is coming up. No, we're not worried about the College Football Playoff or peculiar conference championship game tiebreakers. Our focus is far simpler than that. We are running out of weeks. Now, there's no need to panic. We know the drill; we've been here before. All we can do now is enjoy every remaining minute and make the most of the games we have. As we dive deep into Week 12, this mentality has never felt more real. With Thanksgiving around the corner, things are heating up. Our picks, after a few "meh" weeks, need to pick up, too. Here's what we like in Week 12. Last Week's Record: 5-6 Year to Date: 55-51-1 All point spreads courtesy of FanDuel LSU at Tennessee (Under 45.5) Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We haven't bet many totals this year. We're changing that in this spot. It's been a rollercoaster at LSU, and we're not just talking about the season. The narrative surrounding the coach and quarterback have escalated, and the vibes are not great after a crushing loss against Texas. Once again, the Tigers had no shortage of opportunities to beat a team handily. Once again, turnovers and missed opportunities proved to be the difference. In particular, Sam Leavitt's three interceptions doomed this team. His six red-zone interceptions this season have likely cost LSU a shot at the playoff. As for Tennessee, the team is winning ugly. That's not a bad thing. Right now, given the lack of star power at quarterback, it's actually a wonderful thing. The offensive line is solid, the running game is unrelenting and, best of all, they have largely found a way to win regardless of the opposition. As for this game, it just feels ugly. Tennessee wants to hang onto the ball, LSU might not have maximum motivation and the end result could be a sloppy, tight football game. The Pick: Under 45.5 Michigan (+4) vs. UCLA Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If you have bet against UCLA this season, you have not done well. In fact, until last weekend, you had lost each and every bet you've made. We've been on the wrong side a few times this season; we've also been on the right side. Through it all, the Bruins have stayed unbeaten. Ty Dieffenbach has played a significant role in making this possible. Once the backup QB, Dieffenbach was named the starter when Nico Iamaleava was lost for the season due to injury. Last week, Dieffenbach left his team's game against Illinois with what appeared to be a shoulder issue. He was also walking with a limp. Despite the issues, Dieffenbach returned and helped guide his team to another win. Michigan was throttled by Oregon 31-7, totaling just 286 yards. Both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood played, but neither played well. It was the latest ugly performance for the Wolverines in a season of ugly performances. Despite that showing, look at this point spread. With a total in the 30s, this feels like a low-scoring, ugly football game, regardless of who Michigan starts at QB. We're not proud of this, but we're sticking with it. The Pick: Michigan (+4) TCU (+6.5) vs. Utah Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College football is a game of speed and ability. It is also, and this is why we love it, a game of emotion. This brings us to Utah, one of the few unbeaten teams remaining. The Utes are coming off a thrilling, late-night win at Arizona that featured seven lead changes. The Wildcats ultimately covered, although the Utes left with the unbeaten season intact. Which brings us to this week and one of the larger hangover spots on the football calendar. Not only did Utah play a thriller on Saturday. The week prior, Utah beat rival BYU at home in a matchup that featured plenty of dramatics. Meanwhile, TCU is nowhere near a perfect football team. In fact, the Horned Frogs are 5-5. Interestingly enough, all five of TCU's losses have come by one score or less. The Horned Frogs also nearly beat Arizona on the road a few weeks ago. In fact, they should have won. With the total hovering in the mid-40s, defenses could be a theme. While TCU doesn't do anything exceptionally well, they're solid in all phases. Playing against a team on a multi-week rollercoaster that will hit the road for the second consecutive week, you'll want to keep an eye on this one. Upset brewing. The Pick: TCU (+6.5) CFB Week 12 Picks 🔮 Latest CFB Odds and Picks ✍️ NFL Week 11 Picks 🔮 Kansas (+5.5) vs. BYU Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the topic of highly rated Big 12 teams facing a precarious spot, enter BYU. One team is 8-2; the other is 4-6. While we recognize how different these two teams are, the oddsmakers think the difference between them, at least in this setting, isn't that unique. The Cougars will hit the road for the last time this season, playing an early football game against an opponent that has been a mixed bag this year. On the topic of road games, BYU lost its previous trips to Utah and Central Florida. It also didn't play particularly well at TCU, winning a close game by a touchdown. For Kansas, what version are we getting? Maybe more specifically, which Isaiah Marshall are we getting? The KU quarterback has sensational athleticism. He's coming off back-to-back games with at least 125 yards rushing. As long as he doesn't turn the ball over, which is a big if at times, he can really produce. On the road for four of its last six games, the Jayhawks should find comfort in playing at home. The defense played well last week, limiting West Virginia to just 262 yards of offense. It will struggle to duplicate that effort against a solid BYU offense, although it should be able to keep up offensively. At the risk of repeating ourselves, we'll say it once more. Don't be shocked if we see an upset here. The Pick: Kansas (+5.5) Baylor (+3.5) vs. Texas Tech Chris Gardner/Getty Images Are you sensing a theme? We promise this isn't by design. More than anything, our picks this week highlight the Big 12's sheer absurdity and volatility. While the conference's best teams have largely avoided carnage, that could very well change. As for the opponent, Baylor has certainly had plenty of highs and lows. When Dave Aranda was fired, Joe Klanderman was named interim coach. Until last week, when his team lost by three touchdowns to BYU, things were progressing nicely. Quarterback DJ Lagway has played significantly better football. He should be able to test a Texas Tech defense that isn't the same unit we saw a season ago. Still, the Red Raiders were excellent last week against Oklahoma State. Quarterback Thomas Castellanos was particularly sharp. His arrival has been nothing short of season-saving. Despite that performance, Baylor feels very much alive. Another week on the road against another quarterback with loads of physical talent could present a much different outcome than the one we just saw. Want to see carnage in the Big 12? We're not asking for it, but we might see it. The Pick: Baylor (+3.5) Other Games on the Card Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Missouri (-5.5) vs. Kentucky Last week wasn't fun for either team, although Kentucky has scored just 20 points over its last two games. Missouri has struggled lately, though playing two of the nation's best teams hasn't helped. It'll look much better this week. Army (-5.5) vs. East Carolina While East Carolina has won three consecutive games, they were against Temple, USF, and Charlotte. Army has lost two in a row, although one of those losses came against Memphis. This feels like a get-right moment. Navy (+3.5) vs. Memphis Navy's No. 3-ranked rushing attack is facing off against Memphis' No. 126-ranked rushing defense. That could spell trouble. It's been a rough year for Navy as a whole, but this could change that narrative.
