away.blurb: Star junior tight end Trey'Dez Green is no longer listed on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 21, signaling his possible return to the field for No. 17 LSU (5-2, 2-2 SEC). His removal from the injury report means Green (6-7, 240) will be available to play against Auburn (4-2, 2-2) inside Jordan-Hare Stadium Saturday (11 a.m. CT, ABC). Initially, his injury was feared to be worse than what it ended up being. But his possible return to action after just four weeks is quicker than it was projected. Two weeks ago, Kiffin said that Green was "getting closer" to returning. "If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people think, it would be him," Kiffin said. "He is out of the brace and moving it. So, getting closer." Freshman defensive lineman Richard Anderson is the new name to the injury report for LSU, and he is listed as doubtful. LSU has had rough injury luck this season with major key players getting hurt. Senior linebacker Whit Weeks fractured his fibula during the Texas A&M three weeks ago and his return to the field is uncertain. Junior safety Dashawn Spears suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Ole Miss game. Green sprained his knee in the game against Ole Miss a month ago and has missed the last four games for Lane Kiffin and LSU. As it stands, LSU will be without four players for sure against Auburn in Weeks, Spears, wide receiver Phillip Wright III and linebacker Charles Ross II. away.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
away.blurb: LSU football LB Whit Weeks could be out for the year, according to a report from CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Weeks has been out since leaving LSU's Week 4 win over Texas A&M after fracturing his right fibula. If Weeks is done in 2026, he would miss LSU's final two games, at Tennessee and Arkansas. Weeks, the fourth-year linebacker, is one of LSU's best defenders when he's on the field, but injuries have limited Weeks over the last two seasons. With Weeks out, LSU has leaned on Davhon Keys and TJ Dottery at the linebacker position. Dottery has continued to be one of the SEC's best linebackers. Keys is an impact player vs the run, but isn't as good as Weeks was in pass coverage or rushing the passer. Jhase Thomas being listed as probable likely means that he is expected to play, but did not practice fully on Wednesday. As for Tennessee, they have 10 players listed as out. The big news, though, is that quarterback George MacIntyre is not listed. He left their game last weekend against Texas A&M in the 3rd quarter with a knee injury and did not return. Tennessee comes in to Saturday’s contest ranked #9 and 8-2, while LSU fell out of the rankings following last week’s last second loss to Texas that dropped them to 6-4. Their next test comes against the Tennessee Volunteers , and the Tigers could be without a couple of key receivers. It's Wednesday night, which means the conference released injury reports for each team. There's a long list of Volunteers players who won't be playing in this game, and LSU had a couple of people added. Here's the full list for both teams: Harris has six touchdowns over the last four games. He has become one of the top options for Sam Leavitt all over the field, but especially in the red zone. Watkins' production has slowed to a halt over the past couple of weeks, but he is still their top option in the slot. The biggest news here for Tennessee is that quarterback George MacIntyre is not on the report after he had to leave their last game early. MacIntyre took over starting duties earlier this season. The rushing attack is the focus of their gameplan, but they still need a quaterback they trust. The sophomore has completed 67.9% of his passes this season for 962 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions. He's averaged 162.8 yards per game since starting. Another key loss for the Volunteers is Nic Moore, who had to miss their last game as well. Moore had been up-and-down this year, but he was a starter. Shamurad Umarov will start in his place.

Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs (Jerome Miron, USA TODAY Sports) Trevor Trowbridge · Roundtable Sports Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time since 1989, the Notre Dame Fighting Irish will host the SMU Mustangs inside of Notre Dame Stadium. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. 2026 Week 12 Preview: SMU Mustangs @ Notre Dame Fighting Irish
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: SMU Mustangs @ Notre Dame Fighting Irish | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 19, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC SMU has responded to losses with excellent poise. However, a trip to South Bend is a tough order. Time and date: Saturday, November 21 at 7:30 p.m. ET Location: Notre Dame Stadium — South Bend, IN Spread: Notre Dame (-20.5) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: Notre Dame leads, 10-3 Last meeting: Notre Dame 59, SMU 6 — November 11, 1989 Current streak: Notre Dame, 3 (1986-89) Setting the scene How does SMU respond to a loss? Especially a rare home defeat in which the Mustangs trailed 42-0 at halftime and effectively watched their ACC championship aspirations evaporate? The Mustangs have responded with tremendous poise under head coach Rhett Lashlee, who has not dropped consecutive regular season matchups since his inaugural campaign in 2022. But this isn’t just any follow-up matchup. Immediately after facing 9-1 Wake Forest, SMU must travel to South Bend and take on another 9-1 opponent in Notre Dame. SMU just suffered its first regular season defeat without holding a second half lead since 2023. Now, the Mustangs enter Saturday’s matchup as three-touchdown underdogs against one of the nation’s premier programs. A chance to deliver the ultimate bounce-back statement awaits at Notre Dame Stadium. SMU Mustangs outlook Last Saturday, SMU (7-3, 5-3 ACC) endured a series of unwanted firsts. The Mustangs lost their first-ever ACC matchup at home. The Mustangs suffered their first-ever home loss in ACC play and their first conference defeat by more than 10 points, falling 49-7 to Wake Forest after an uncompetitive first half. The road to redemption won’t get any easier against Notre Dame. However, the potential reward is even greater than last week’s setback, as SMU can secure its first victory over an AP Top 5 opponent since defeating No. 2 Texas in 1980. Program icon Kevin Jennings looks to author a signature performance before exhausting his eligibility. The fifth-year senior quarterback ranks seventh nationally in passing yards, sitting 27 yards shy of his third-straight 3,000-yard season. He’s also fifth in the country with 26 passing touchdowns. Most impressively, Jennings operates with some of the highest efficiency in the FBS. His 62.9 completion rate last week was his lowest of the season, and he ranks third nationally, connecting on 72.6 percent of attempts. SMU’s 15th-ranked offense can be as dynamic and explosive as any in the country, but that was not the case last week when it registered just 47 yards across its first six possessions. Wake Forest largely eliminated the Mustangs’ run game from the onset, forced early turnovers, and provided significant pressure on dropbacks. Part of the challenge has been integrating a revamped offensive line. SMU recently inserted two true freshmen into starting roles on the left side while retaining veterans Joshua Bates, Addison Nichols (who is questionable), and PJ Williams at center, right guard, and right tackle, respectively. That unit faces a formidable test against Notre Dame’s defensive front. The Mustangs’ rushing attack has been volatile this season. Starting running back Kendrick Raphael has eclipsed 100 yards three times in ACC play, but there were three other conference games where the entire ground game was held below 70 yards, including last week. Raphael remains the workhorse tailback, but freshman Christian Rhodes has gotten increasingly involved, generating 92 rushing yards two weeks ago against Virginia Tech. SMU features an abundance of capable playmakers in its receiving corps. Four Mustangs have at least 30 receptions on the season, led by Yamir Knight’s 56 catches for 670 yards and six touchdowns. Yannick Smith and Jalen Cooper are among other downfield threats, while tight end Randy Pittman Jr. has been a consistent intermediate target all season. This group supplies much of the offense’s explosive potential, helping SMU rank fifth nationally with seven 50+ yard completions this season. The Mustangs only surrendered more than 30 points once before last week. The defensive line had proven overwhelming against several ACC opponents, but Wake Forest managed to neutralize that advantage. SMU ranks 20th nationally and third in the conference with 2.8 sacks per game, spearheaded by Marques White. The eighth-year senior defensive end leads all ACC defenders with 8.5 sacks, while adding 12.0 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries in a standout season. SMU struggled containing the run game last week, and the defense has been middle-of-the-road in that department this year. The passing defense, meanwhile, has made significant strides since 2025, although it recently experienced a major setback. Safety Jimmy Wyrick is out for the year, joining Tyren Polley Jr. as the second starting safety to suffer a season-ending injury. However, reigning First Team All-ACC selection Ahmaad Moses, who was granted an injunction for temporary eligibility, will make his second appearance of the season after debuting against Wake Forest. Moses had five interceptions last year, including two against SMU’s most recent top-10 opponent, Miami (FL). As heavy road underdogs at Notre Dame, SMU can’t just rely on stops. The Mustangs need to ramp up their turnover output after producing just three interceptions in their first 10 games. Notre Dame Fighting Irish outlook Notre Dame (9-1, Independent) is continuing its College Football Playoff pursuit after missing the field in 2025. The Fighting Irish secured a signature win Nov. 7 against otherwise-undefeated Miami (FL), staving off a late comeback to put themselves in prime playoff position. Outside of close finishes against current top-10 opponents Miami (FL) and BYU, the Fighting Irish have demolished the competition. Their other eight victories all came by double-digits, and North Carolina was the only other opponent to finish within 17 points. Following off a 34-point annihilation of Boston College, Notre Dame currently ranks first in point differential against FBS opponents at +25.6 per game. Quarterback CJ Carr enjoyed a promising debut season last year, but the junior has taken another significant step forward in 2026. His completion percentage has ballooned to 67.9, his passing yards per game output has climbed by 10, and he has delivered an efficient 24 touchdowns against two interceptions. Given the lopsided nature of most Notre Dame games, the quarterback hasn’t been shouldered with a heavy load in second halves. But when he needed to come through against Miami (FL), he did with a season-high 319 passing yards along with three touchdowns. Carr is supported by the wide receiver duo of Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert, who are nearly identical in production this season. Faison has 615 receiving yards and six touchdowns, while Gilbert presents 614 yards and six scores. Recently, Gilbert has taken command of the offense, recording 14 receptions for 184 yards and three touchdowns across his last two starts. That doesn’t mean Faison has faded into the background, and he found the end zone in both of those ACC victories. Replicating last year’s run game was never going to be easy after losing two first-round NFL Draft picks, but the Fighting Irish are steadily reestablishing an identity on the ground. They produced a 100-yard rusher in four of their last six outings. Much like the receiving corps, the running back room is driven by a duo with similar statistics and similar builds. Jonaz Walton has 655 rushing yards on the season, and he’s been the more explosive with 7.0 yards per carry. Meanwhile, Nolan James Jr. follows closely with 644 rushing yards, and his 10 touchdowns are tied for 18th in the country. But the underlying catalyst for Carr and the run game’s success is arguably the best offensive line in the country. Notre Dame ranks first nationally in fewest sacks allowed, surrendering just three through 10 games. The line, anchored by potential All-American gaurd Anthonie Knapp, has also surrendered the fewest tackles for loss and yardage from tackles for loss in the FBS. As dominant as Notre Dame’s seventh-ranked scoring offense has been, its fifth-ranked scoring defense has been equally as imposing. The Fighting Irish surrender just 13.8 points per game and lead the FBS in total defense, allowing a mere 240 yards per contest. Only three teams managed more to score more than 13 points against this unit — BYU (28), North Carolina (26), and Miami (FL) (24). Although Notre Dame hasn’t generated sacks at the highest rate, its defensive front has consistently disrupted opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Boubacar Traore leads the charge with 5.0 sacks, 8.0 tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles, while his counterpart Bryce Young has registered 4.0 sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss. The Fighting Irish will be shorthanded at the next level, however, as inside linebacker Drayk Bowen remains out for the third-straight game. Rounding out an imposing defense is reigning unanimous All-American cornerback Leonard Moore. After intercepting five passes last season, Moore has yet to record a pick in 2026. That doesn’t mean opposing quarterbacks have found success targeting him. Rather, his presence has deterred passers from looking in his direction, and he has done a standup job locking up WR1s all season. Even against one of the highest-ranked opponents on the road, it is nearly impossible for things to go worse for SMU than they did last week. The Mustangs should enter South Bend with renewed urgency and considerably more competitiveness on both sides of the ball, keeping the matchup within reach through several quarters. Kevin Jennings is as great of a passer as Notre Dame will face this season, alsongside with Darian Mensah. SMU possesses enough offensive firepower to become just the fourth team to surpass 13 points against this remarkably stingy defense. However, the Mustangs will need to find production in multiple areas to remain competitive. Notre Dame holds significant advantages elsewhere, particularly in the trenches. The Fighting Irish’s dominant offensive line should provide CJ Carr ample time to survey SMU’s secondary while opening running lanes for a backfield that has become increasingly productive as of late. That combination could prove overwhelming for a Mustangs defense that surrendered 49 points last week. SMU will put up a much better fight than it did against Wake Forest, but Notre Dame’s physicality will take over. The Fighting Irish withstand one of their tougher tests and continue the trek toward their fourth CFP appearance since 2018. What should Fighting Irish fans expect in South Bend? Notre Dame football is two wins away from a College Football Playoff berth. The Fighting Irish host the SMU Mustangs at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in Notre Dame Stadium , and head coach Marcus Freeman's group needs to take care of business against SMU and then Syracuse to finish 11-1. It is also Senior Day. Hopefully the Irish land a home game in the playoff. Even so, this could be the last time this senior class walks out of the tunnel, hits the Play Like a Champion Today sign, and plays in front of the Notre Dame crowd. At one point, SMU looked like it would give Notre Dame's resume a nice bump. That changed after Wake Forest throttled the Mustangs last weekend. SMU trailed 42-0 at halftime and lost 49-7. This won't be the top-25 resume boost many expected, but Notre Dame still has plenty to play for. A decisive win could push the Irish up a couple more spots as the season winds down. Notre Dame is a 90% favorite to win outright in the Kalshi prediction market. The Irish are favored by 20.5 points, which is roughly three touchdowns, and Kalshi gives them a 51% chance of covering that number. I like both, and I especially like Notre Dame to cover. Don't expect a Senior Day hangover Some people will look at this game and point to Senior Day, a potential hangover, and the other usual distractions. I just find it unlikely that Notre Dame won't be locked in and ready to play. We had the same conversation heading into the Boston College game after the Irish beat No. 1 Miami. Notre Dame was cool, calm, and collected, and the team was ready early. Slow first halves have popped up occasionally during Freeman's tenure, but we didn't see one last week. SMU is also substantially better than Boston College. I don't want anyone to underrate the Mustangs because of the Wake Forest result. That game was a bit of an anomaly. This is still a quality 7-3 team, and if SMU had been on a bye last week, we would feel a whole lot different about this matchup. Should Notre Dame win convincingly? Absolutely. Can the Irish show up with their C or D game and cruise? I don't think so. Kevin Jennings and the SMU passing game SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings has been really good outside of a couple of bad games. He is one of the better passers in college football and has developed steadily over the last couple of years. He has some dual-threat ability, but he wants to stay inside of structure and win from the pocket. I don't think Jennings is going to have back-to-back stinkers. SMU has some good receivers on the outside, including Jaylen Cooper. Notre Dame fans may remember Cooper from the 2025 recruiting class, when the Irish tried to flip him from SMU. The Notre Dame secondary will be tested. The Irish are still without DJ McKinney, but will have Jayden Sanders and Leonard Moore available. There are obviously good pieces on the back end, but the Mustangs have the potential to create a couple of explosive plays in the passing game. What keeps SMU from scoring a ton of points is the run game. It has been wildly inconsistent. The Mustangs have run for 250 yards in some games and fewer than 100 in others. An offense that isn't balanced will struggle to sustain drives against a defense this good, and SMU's feast-or-famine passing attack figures to be spotty. What to watch from the Notre Dame offense SMU's offense can be dangerous, but its defense is not good. That gives Notre Dame a chance to keep building on what has been working. I want to see the run game continue to ascend, so keep riding Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton . Quarterback CJ Carr can add a few more explosives through the air and play a little more consistently. The bigger thing I'll be watching is how Notre Dame starts each half. The Irish have gotten off to fast starts more consistently recently, and that needs to continue. Against Boston College, Notre Dame put up a 24-point second quarter, then opened the second half with an interception. Winning those middle eights and coming out of the locker room with some juice is another massive key. Notre Dame vs. SMU score prediction I expect SMU to score some points, but 17 feels like about the best the Mustangs can do without a sudden breakthrough in the run game. I think Notre Dame starts to take control somewhere in the second quarter and stays in command throughout the second half. Final score prediction: Notre Dame 41, SMU 17 That covers the spread and gives the Irish the decisive victory they need. If they handle business on Saturday, only Syracuse stands between Notre Dame and a playoff berth. away.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. away.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Brauntae Johnson, junior safety for Notre Dame football, was upgraded to questionable for Senior Night this week against Southern Methodist after missing nine full games due to left foot surgery. The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Analysis: Play by play, Notre Dame football keeps it eyes on the prize Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. home.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
home.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. home.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
home.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Brauntae Johnson, junior safety for Notre Dame football, was upgraded to questionable for Senior Night this week against Southern Methodist after missing nine full games due to left foot surgery. The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Analysis: Play by play, Notre Dame football keeps it eyes on the prize Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. picks.headline: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back?
picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NFL suspends Rams WR Puka Nacua 3 games TRENDING TNF preview: Texans have hope? Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. picks.headline: Missouri Offense Preview: Can Kentucky slow Tigers talent?
picks.blurb: Missouri Offense Preview: Can Kentucky slow Tigers talent? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NFL suspends Rams WR Puka Nacua 3 games TRENDING TNF preview: Texans have hope? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 18, 2026 at 10:18 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is coming off back-to-back losses and the Wildcats defense have to prepare for one of the most dangerous offenses in the SEC. Missouri is statistically one of the most explosive offenses in the conference. The Tigers have one of the best quarterbacks in the conference, maybe the best duo at wide receiver in the SEC and one of two running backs in the conference that has already rushed for over 1,000 yards. Kentucky's defense has to come ready to play on the road. We will start with the dynamic lefty quarterback, Austin Simmons, Simmons has 19 touchdowns and just three interceptions on the season. Simmons has thrown for 2,381 passing yards this season and he is constantly pushing the football downfield, his 10.1 average depth of target ranks second in the SEC. He has a 12.3 explosive pass rate, which ranks 4th among SEC quarterbacks. Not to mention, Simmons has been sacked just eight times this season, which is the fewest among starting quarterbacks in the SEC; Simmons doesn't escape sacks like a LaNorris Sellers but he does an incredible job at getting the football out on time. When you look at the advanced stats provided by Clark Brooks of secstatcat.com, these numbers tell a different story that could benefit the Wildcats defense. Simmons is getting a lot of what we would call "turnover luck" this season as he has just three interceptions on the season. However, according to Clark Brooks charting, Simmons has thrown 26 passes this season that could have been intercepted. Kentucky's defense has not forced a turnover after the bye week despite thriving in that area before the bye week, it would be extremely beneficial if the pendulum could swing back in the Wildcats favor in this game and is something to watch. Simmons pushes the football down the field to his top target that also transferred over with him to Missouri from Ole Miss, Cayden Lee. Lee leads the SEC in receptions (65), receiving yards (879) and yards per game (87.9). Lee has five touchdowns on the year and is one of the most dynamic slot receivers in the country. They also have a big playmaker on the outside with Donovan Olugbode, he has 47 catches for 691 yards and 8 touchdowns on the season. Olugbode ranks top six among SEC wide receivers in yards, touchdowns and yards per game. His 6-foot-2, 210-pound frame pairs really well with a dynamic slot receiver like Lee. These are Simmons two go-to guys and he will target his tight ends at times as well. This is one of the most dangerous passing attacks the Wildcats have faced all season, so the secondary will have to play one of their best games of the season in Columbia. Then that brings us to Jamal Roberts, the running back who has filled in for Ahmad Hardy while he was sidelined for a majority of the season. Roberts has been unbelievable as the lead back, he is second in the SEC with 228 carries, 1,133 rushing yards and 113 rushing yards per game. Roberts has 9 rushing touchdowns on the year and he is averaging 4.97 yards per carry. If Roberts is getting the running game going paired with Simmons ability to hit downfield throws, this Tigers offense can be a lot to handle. Missouri is also coming off back-to-back losses to Texas and Georgia, creating a fascinating football game under the lights in CoMo. The Tigers offense struggled last week on the road in Athens and they missed opportunities in the fourth quarter to upset Texas at home the week before. Kentucky's offense has scored just 20 points in the last eight quarters of play. Which offense will show up and bounce back will be the difference in this football game. picks.headline: BY THE NUMBERS: Previewing Kentucky vs. Missouri
Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 19, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.headline: How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. After Wilson Berry punted for four games (averaging 42.6 yards a kick), UK went back to its original starting punter of 2026, Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara , vs. the Gators. O’Hara kicked three times vs. UF and averaged 46.3 yards a kick. On the season, O’Hara, an Australian, has averaged 41.5 yards on 20 punts. • Missouri place-kicker Blake Craig has missed nine of his 24 field-goal tries this season but has a long make of 53 yards. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. All-SEC Georgia star's status in doubt vs. Missouri
home.blurb: However, Georgia has two new players that popped up on the injury report. Georgia starting center Drew Bobo, an All-SEC pick, is doubtful to play. It is unclear what Bobo's injury is, but if he misses the game, then that would be significant for the Georgia offensive line, which is coming off a dominant performance against Ole Miss. Georgia missed Bobo last year in the SEC championship and the postseason. He's a critical part of the Georgia offense. Up front, Georgia's Josh Horton is questionable. Horton is a new player listed on the injury report and has seven tackles and two sacks this season. Pass rusher Amaris Williams remains out for Georgia after tearing his ACL in spring practice. Georgia has some banged up players that aren't on the injury report. Running back Dante Dowdell remains out and running back Chauncey Bowens did not play against Ole Miss despite not having an injury designation. "He's not 100%," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on Bowens. "Just because someone is dressed out and cleared does not mean that they're able to go out there and play and perform. He's working his tail off to get back." Out: Linebacker Amaris Williams (torn ACL) Out: Running back Dante Dowdell (upper body) Questionable: Defensive lineman Josh Horton Out: Offensive lineman Josh Atkins Missouri star quarterback Austin Simmons and receiver Cayden Lee do not appear on the Tigers' availability report. Both players needed medical assistance during the Missouri loss to Texas, but appear to be able to play against Georgia. 'GTA 6' impacts sports Dawg Post Matt DeBary · Georgia Bulldogs On SI Sat, November 14, 2026 at 6:47 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads ATHENS - The No. 1 ranked Georgia Bulldogs are back home hosting the No. 22 ranked Missouri Tigers . Kirby Smart and the Dawgs are coming off a dominant 42-7 led by a five-touchdown performance from Gunner Stockton and another elite performance from the Bulldog defense . This is Georgia's first game back in Athens since their headscratching loss to Auburn before the open week in mid-October. Final Score: Georgia - 48 Missouri - 21 (12:53) - With backup Ryan Puglisi in at quarterback, the Bulldog offense does not slow down. After Puglisi hit receiver Talyn Taylor for a 29-yard gain, running back Chauncey Bowens, who hasn't played since the Vanderbilt game, scores a 4th quarter touchdown to extend Georgia's lead. (6:15) - The Bulldog defense gets another stop and the offense takes advantage with their fifth touchdown of the game. Nate Frazier runs it in for his third score of the game and the Bulldogs add on. (10:42) - The Bulldogs drive almost the length of the field on their first offensive drive in the second half that resulted in a 40-yard field goal by Peyton Woodring. away.blurb: Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. away.headline: What's TCU quarterback's status for the showdown with No. 2 Utah?
away.blurb: TCU football is expecting senior quarterback Jaden Craig to be available against No. 2 Utah on Saturday. While Craig will be available on Saturday, it appears he still not be 100% and that means the Horned Frogs could rely on sophomore quarterback Adam Schobel. Schobel played about half a dozen snaps against the Wildcats, rushing for three yards on three carries. “I love Adam; we came in at the same time. home.headline: What's TCU quarterback's status for the showdown with No. 2 Utah?
home.blurb: TCU football is expecting senior quarterback Jaden Craig to be available against No. 2 Utah on Saturday. While Craig will be available on Saturday, it appears he still not be 100% and that means the Horned Frogs could rely on sophomore quarterback Adam Schobel. Schobel played about half a dozen snaps against the Wildcats, rushing for three yards on three carries. “I love Adam; we came in at the same time. He was a freshman when I transferred in,” Pimpton said. “So I have a great relationship with Adam. I’m pretty sure Jay’s going to tough it and play. He’s gonna go out there and do his thing regardless. Whoever goes out there, we will ride behind him no matter what goes on.” Craig was hobbled during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kansas State last Saturday with a lower body injury, but is expected to be a full-go when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) host the Utes (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. on Fox . “I would expect him to play,” TCU head coach Sonny Dykes said Tuesday. “He was a lot better today than he was yesterday, and so I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” If Schobel has to play more against Utah, Dykes doesn’t anticipate the offense needing to change much to fit his skillset. “I think Adam’s a little more mobile than Jaden, and so that would change, but not really,” Dykes said. “The playbook wouldn’t change much. Adam’s been repping our offense all fall camp and all season. So he can go in and execute what we need if we needed him to.” If Schobel gets a bigger role against the Utes, he’ll have the full support of his teammates, like senior tight end Ka’Morreun Pimpton.
